html:
The Black Hawk War was a short war in 1832 in Illinois and what is now Wisconsin, between the United States and a band of Sauk, Meskwaki and Kickapoo led by the Sauk war leader Black Hawk.

A treaty of 1804, which the Sauk and Meskwaki said had been signed by men with no right to sell, gave away their lands east of the Mississippi. When settlers took over the main Sauk town, most of the Sauk and Meskwaki moved west into Iowa. In April 1832 Black Hawk led about a thousand people, many of them women and children, back across the river, hoping for help from other nations and the British.

The help never came. Illinois militia, among them a young Abraham Lincoln, and army troops chased the band through Illinois and Wisconsin. After an early win at Stillman's Run, Black Hawk's people were worn down by hunger. On 1 and 2 August, as they tried to cross back over the Mississippi at the Bad Axe River, soldiers and a gunboat killed hundreds of them.

Black Hawk surrendered, was jailed and then shown around eastern cities, and dictated an autobiography. The war sped up removal under the Indian Removal Act: the Sauk and Meskwaki had to give up eastern Iowa, and the Ho-Chunk lost land in Wisconsin. Their descendants include the Sac and Fox Nation of Oklahoma.
sum: The Black Hawk War was a short war in 1832 in Illinois and what is now Wisconsin, between the United States and a band of Sauk, Meskwaki and Kickapoo led by the Sauk war leader Black Hawk.
